how_to_obtain.instruction: Review recovery tooling access control configuration and test whether a user with only 'Recovery Operator' permissions can execute a restore without a separate approver sign-off.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Test execution blocked with error 'Approval required from Recovery Approver role'; or documented evidence in change control log that all recovery jobs have a corresponding approval record with approver identity and timestamp.

option_description: Defines the mechanism used to restrict who can initiate, approve, or execute data recovery operations and interact with recovery tooling. Valid options are role-based access control (rbac), attribute-based access control (abac), manual approval only (manual_approval_only), or no formal control in place (none).
security_impact: The Rego policy rule 'role_based_recovery_authorization_control' only activates its countermeasure when recovery_access_control_type is set to 'rbac' or 'abac', combined with recovery_roles_defined == true and recovery_approval_workflow_enforced == true. Without rbac or abac, the countermeasure score of 2 is not applied, leaving recovery tooling exposed to unauthorized or accidental restoration operations. This matters because uncontrolled access to recovery tooling can allow threat actors or misconfigured automation to overwrite live data with stale backups, exfiltrate backup contents, or deny recovery capability entirely.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect IAM policies attached to backup and recovery tooling (e.g., AWS Backup, Azure Recovery Services, or GCP Backup) to determine whether role-based or attribute-based conditions govern access.
how_to_obtain.command: aws iam list-policies --scope Local --query 'Policies[?contains(PolicyName, `Backup`) || contains(PolicyName, `Recovery`)].{Name:PolicyName,Arn:Arn}' --output table && aws iam list-roles --query 'Roles[?contains(RoleName, `Backup`) || contains(RoleName, `Recovery`)].{Role:RoleName,Arn:Arn}' --output table
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A list of IAM policies and roles scoped to backup/recovery operations. If roles are present with condition keys (e.g., aws:PrincipalTag or aws:RequestedRegion), abac is in use. If roles are present without condition-based policies, rbac is in use. If neither is present, control type is likely none.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Navigate to the cloud provider's backup service console to verify whether access is governed by defined roles or attribute conditions. For AWS Backup: open the AWS Console, go to AWS Backup > Settings > Access Policies. For Azure: open Recovery Services Vault > Access Control (IAM) and review role assignments.
how_to_obtain.navigation: AWS Console > AWS Backup > Settings > Access Policies | Azure Portal > Recovery Services Vault > Access Control (IAM) > Role Assignments | GCP Console > Backup and DR > IAM > Roles
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Presence of named roles (e.g., BackupOperator, RecoveryApprover) assigned to specific principals indicates rbac. Conditional role bindings based on tags or attributes indicate abac. Absence of structured assignments indicates none or manual_approval_only.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the backup/recovery operations team and review any documented access control procedures or change management records to determine whether recovery initiation requires role-based authorization or goes through a manual approval workflow (e.g., ticketing system, change advisory board).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: If recovery requires ticket approval or a CAB review without any technical enforcement in tooling, classify as manual_approval_only. If no formal process exists, classify as none. If tooling enforces role or attribute restrictions programmatically, classify as rbac or abac accordingly.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review Terraform, CloudFormation, or Pulumi IaC files defining backup and recovery infrastructure to identify whether IAM role bindings or ABAC condition blocks are present in the resource definitions.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Files containing role definitions with Condition blocks referencing tag-based attributes indicate abac. Files with role assignments to named groups or service accounts without conditions indicate rbac. No relevant files or empty results suggest none or manual_approval_only.
